description:
Trigger: every call to CrlChecker::new_with_signer_discovery (pkix-revocation/src/crl.rs:325-358).

The `cert_to_check: &Certificate` parameter is declared in the public signature (currently spelled `_cert_to_check` to silence the unused-variable lint) and the rustdoc (lines 281-288) explicitly says: 'It is taken at construction time only for ergonomic symmetry with the discovery flow; the actual revocation lookup happens at check_revocation call time. Passing a different cert argument to check_revocation later is well-defined.'

This is API surface that has zero behavioral effect today. Two consequences for the maintainer:

1. Future-self forgetting: in 12 months, a caller will rely on the parameter (perhaps believing it pre-validates the CRL covers cert_to_check) and the code will silently ignore it. They will file an issue about 'why doesn't new_with_signer_discovery reject when I pass the wrong cert.'

2. Post-1.0 lock-in: the parameter is part of the function signature. Removing it post-1.0 is a breaking change. Adding behavior to it post-1.0 is a behavior change that prior callers (who pass any cert) may have relied on as a no-op.

Per AGENTS.md 'design for the eventual complete shape' and 'breaking changes are free pre-1.0': decide now.

Options:
1. Remove the parameter entirely. Update the rustdoc to drop the 'ergonomic symmetry' rationale.
2. Make it meaningful: at construction time, check that the CRL is at least syntactically applicable to cert_to_check (e.g., issuer-DN match between cert.issuer and the discovered signer's subject, or run check_idp_dp_scope to fail-fast on out-of-scope CRLs before the caller even calls check_revocation).

Either is fine; the status quo (parameter present, behavior absent, doc explains it's pointless) is the worst of both worlds.
title: new_with_signer_discovery: _cert_to_check parameter is unused, locks API to a no-op arg
